title: Integral multiplication certificate for an algebraic element over a valuation ring
statement: Let $K\subseteq L$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], let $V\subseteq K$ be a valuation subring [def-trf-valuation-ring], and let $C$ be the integral closure of $V$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. For every $x\in L$ there exist $a,b,c,d\in C$ such that $b=xa$, $d=xc$, and $a-d=1$, where the multiplication identities are read inside $L$.

source.place: Agent-written polynomial-tail argument from steps 4--6 of lem-trf-valuation-normalization-localizations, using Stacks Tag 090P (lemma-find-valuation-rings) to recognize integral tails. This reconstructs the normalization background used by Temkin Proposition 2.2.1, converse proof, printed p.11; the multiplication-certificate formulation is not asserted to be a statement in Stacks or Temkin.

proof.text: Choose a nonzero polynomial p over K vanishing at x. Choose a nonzero coefficient p_k of maximal V-valuation on its finite support. By ValuationSubring.valuation_le_iff every p_i/p_k lies in V. Thus q=C(p_k^-1)*p vanishes at x, has all coefficients in V and coefficient q_k=1.

Define q_n by applying Polynomial.divX n times to q, and t_n=q_n(x). Coefficient extraction gives coeff(q_n,i)=coeff(q,i+n), hence x*t_(n+1)+coeff(q_n,0)=t_n, with t_0=0. All the mapped coefficients belong to C.

By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal], C is integrally closed in L. Test in a valuation subring T containing C as in [lem-trf-integral-closure-valuation-intersection]. Induction proves that t_n and x*t_n belong to T. The recurrence puts x*t_(n+1)=t_n-coeff(q_n,0) in T. If x belongs to T, evaluate q_(n+1) using its coefficients in T. Otherwise x^-1 belongs to T and multiplication puts t_(n+1) in T; x=0 is also handled directly by the constant coefficient. Separation by valuation subrings, the first clause of Stacks Tag 090P implemented by Subring.exists_le_valuationSubring_of_isIntegrallyClosedIn, therefore puts t_n and x*t_n in C.

Choose a=t_k, b=x*t_k, c=t_(k+1), d=x*t_(k+1), all in C. The recurrence at k and q_k=1 give a-d=1, and the two multiplication equations hold by construction. The same formulas apply at k=0, at the leading coefficient and at x=0.

lean.statement: theorem integralClosure_mul_certificate (K : Type u) (L : Type v) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] (V : ValuationSubring K) (x : L) : ∃ a b c d : integralClosure V L, (b : L) = x * (a : L) ∧ (d : L) = x * (c : L) ∧ a - d = 1
